1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# check-prover-record.sh — gate (a) of the push gate: a fresh, committed prover record
     3	# dated today must exist before a push, and that record must be fresh for BOTH guarded
     4	# documents — PRODUCT_SPEC.md and ARCHITECTURE.md (SPEC M-6, INV-116: every live-spec push
     5	# is preceded by a fresh re-check recorded in docs/prover/, covering the spec and the
     6	# architecture alike).
     7	#
     8	# ONE RECORD PER PUSH (SPEC INV-304). A push once owed two review records to two separate
     9	# gates: this one, and a second adversarial read of the pushed delta kept in its own home.
    10	# The two are one pass, so they are one record. On the PUSH road this gate therefore also
    11	# holds what the second gate held: the record names the pushed range, carries the fields
    12	# that say what the review covered, and leaves no blocking finding open.
    13	#
    14	# THE LAW behind that half. A change that passes every test can still be wrong in ways no
    15	# test asks about. A reviewer briefed to find reasons to refuse the change reads it
    16	# differently from a reviewer set on confirming it, and the difference is what the suite
    17	# misses. So the record a push carries is an adversarial read of the very commits it sends.
    18	#
    19	# THE RECORD. One dated file under <prover-dir>, committed, carrying:
    20	#   PUSH-REVIEW      the marker line
    21	#   Range:           the base commit and the head commit the review read, with the commits
    22	#                    between them listed under it
    23	#   Files read:      the files the reviewer opened
    24	#   Checks run:      the commands the reviewer ran, each with its result
    25	#   Findings:        what the review found; a review that found nothing says so here, and its
    26	#                    coverage stands on the two fields above
    27	#   Blocking:        `none`, or one item per blocking finding, each carrying `closed:` or
    28	#                    `stands:` with the reason it stands
    29	# docs/prover/README.md holds the same shape for a person writing one, and holds no field
    30	# this script leaves unread.
    31	#
    32	# WHAT THIS SCRIPT CAN HOLD: that a record exists, that it is committed rather than a scratch
    33	# file, that it is fresh against the guarded documents and against the pushed range, that it
    34	# names the base commit and every reviewed commit, that it carries each field with a value,
    35	# and that a blocking finding is closed or explained.
    36	#
    37	# WHAT THIS SCRIPT CANNOT HOLD: whether the review was adversarial. No script decides whether
    38	# a reviewer set out to refuse the change or to confirm it, whether the files named were read,
    39	# or whether the findings are the ones the delta deserved. Those rest on the reviewer. This
    40	# gate applies the pressure a machine can apply — the record names the commits, the files, the
    41	# checks and the findings — and leaves the judgment where it belongs.
    42	#
    43	# Usage: check-prover-record.sh [--push] [prover-dir] [YYYY-MM-DD]
    44	#   prover-dir  defaults to docs/prover (relative to the repo root)
    45	#   date        defaults to today
    46	#
    47	# "Present and committed" means: at least one file matching <prover-dir>/<date>*.md
    48	# both exists on disk AND is tracked by git (git ls-files sees it) — not just an
    49	# untracked scratch file sitting in the working tree.
    50	#
    51	# Freshness rule (row 61, SPEC M-6; extended row 271, INV-116): a record dated-today-and-
    52	# committed is not enough on its own — it can be a record for a STALE state if PRODUCT_SPEC.md
    53	# or ARCHITECTURE.md changed again after it landed. So after the tracked-record check above
    54	# passes, also require that the newest commit touching <prover-dir> is at least as new as the
    55	# newest commit touching PRODUCT_SPEC.md, and separately at least as new as the newest commit
    56	# touching ARCHITECTURE.md (equal, or the document's commit is an ancestor of the record's
    57	# commit — a record may ship in the very same commit as the document change it covers).
    58

    60	
    61	REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null || pwd)"
    62	cd "$REPO_ROOT"
    63	
    64	# Two roads (row 571, the cost audit's repair b). The PUSH road (--push; pre-push and CI pass
    65	# it) keeps the original demand: a record dated today. The default WORK road serves an ordinary
    66	# suite run: a clean tree after midnight is not a defect, so it also accepts the newest committed
    67	# record of any date — the freshness checks below still refuse it the moment PRODUCT_SPEC.md or
    68	# ARCHITECTURE.md changed after it.
    69	PUSH_ROAD=0
    70	if [ "${1:-}" = "--push" ]; then
    71	  PUSH_ROAD=1
    72	  shift
    73	fi
